props.name: label
props.description: What the wait is, announced to screen readers in place of the silent ring. "Loading" is the honest default; "Saving draft…" is the better one.

props.name: size
props.description: Ring diameter, from the icon-size tokens so the spinner matches the icon beside it. Not the `size` prop's height scale: a spinner is a circle, and a circle's size is its diameter.

props.name: status
props.description: Announces progress when it is known, e.g. "Uploading 60%".

ai.summary: A spinning ring for an operation in progress, announced to screen readers by its label rather than by the moving picture.
whenToUse: An operation is running and the interface cannot say how far along it is
A button or icon button is in its loading state and needs an inline indicator
whenNotToUse: Progress is measurable — use a Progress bar; a spinner cannot say 60%
Content is loading into a known layout — use a Skeleton, which promises the layout instead of motion
ai.accessibility: Carries `role="status"` so screen readers announce it as a live region. The visible ring is `aria-hidden` — it is a picture of waiting, and `label` (default "Loading") is what gets announced; `status` replaces it when progress is known. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the spin stops rather than slows: a slow spinner still implies movement it cannot show, so the ring freezes solid and the label carries the whole story. Same ruling as Icon Button's loading state — if one changes, both must.
knownLimitations: It cannot express progress fraction — that is a Progress bar's job, not a faster spin
